title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
In the UK in the period January to September (Q1–3) 2026:

Box office revenue was £897 million, up 20% on Q1–3 2025.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
There were 108 million cinema admissions, up 15% on Q1–3 2025.
Figures are for all films on release, including event releases and those that started their release prior to the Q1–3 period.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
August recorded Q1–3 2026’s highest monthly admissions, at 17 million.
Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey were the highest earning releases of that month.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
At the UK and Republic of Ireland (ROI) box office:

Revenue for films released in Q1–3 2026 was £877 million, up 28% on Q1–3 2025.
This excludes event releases.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
The total market share of all UK qualifying films was 44.5%, which is 1.5 percentage points higher than Q1–3 2025’s UK qualifying share.
Note: Figures in chart are rounded and may not sum to quoted value.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
In the UK, in the 12 months to September 2026:

The combined total spend on film and high-end television (HETV) production was £5.18 billion, down 20% on the previous 12-month period.
This graph shows the figures that were ‘first reported’ for production spend in each 12-month period.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
Production data is revised every period to account for lags in obtaining complete data across all types of productions.
Combined spend for the 12 months to September 2026 was down 29% on revised figures for the previous 12-month period.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: HETV accounted for 64% of UK production spend in the 12 months to September 2026.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: UK spend on film production was £1.84 billion for the 12 months ending September 2026, down 33% compared with revised figures for the 12 months ending September 2025.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
The BFI assigns productions to one of three categories:

Inward investment features (INW)
Domestic UK features (DOM)
Co-productions (COP)

See notes to statistics releases for full definitions.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
These graphs plot first reported data against revised data for all productions (ALL) and INW, DOM and COP projects.
Note: Scales on the vertical axes vary by panel to preserve detail within each production category. Panels are not directly comparable by eye – check axis labels.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: UK spend on HETV projects was £3.33 billion in the 12 months to September 2026, down 26% on revised figures for the previous 12-month period.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: Spend on co-productions more than doubled compared with revised figures for the 12 months to September 2025.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
Individual spend figures for first reported INW and COP projects are not shown for the 12 months to September 2022 for reasons of disclosure control.
Note: Scales on the vertical axes vary by panel to preserve detail within each production category. Panels are not directly comparable by eye – check axis labels.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
In the UK, in the 12 months to September 2026:

Combined production starts were up 3% on first reported figures for the 12 months to September 2025.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: Production count for the 12 months to September 2026 is lower than for the other periods shown here. However, as previously noted, figures are likely to be revised upward in subsequent statistical releases as more data becomes available.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: We saw earlier that HETV accounted for the majority of UK production spend in the 12 months to September 2026. In terms of number of productions, however, film accounted for the majority: 54%.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: 188 films were recorded as starting principal photography in the UK in the 12 months to September 2026.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: Lags in obtaining complete data on production activity tend to disproportionately affect counts for domestic UK feature films (DOM), particularly those with budgets of less than £500,000.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: The lag affecting DOM projects can be clearly seen in these graphs, which compare first reported project counts to revised project counts across all categories of production.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: 161 HETV programmes were recorded as starting principal photography in the UK in the 12 months to September 2026.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: HETV programme starts in the 12 months to September 2026 included 13 feature-length single episode productions.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: Individual counts for first reported INW and COP projects are not reported for the 12 months to September 2022 for reasons of disclosure control.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
In the 12 months to September 2026:

A total of 762 films received final certification, either under the cultural test or as an official co-production.
Certification is required to access UK tax reliefs and credits for audiovisual and video game expenditure.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
Films achieving final certification in the 12 months to September 2026 had an associated UK production spend of £2.94 billion.
Films and other productions can apply for final certification when they have completed production and are ready to be released.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
263 HETV titles received final certification through the cultural test in the 12 months to September 2026.
There were two co-productions with final certification but details are not included for disclosure control reasons.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: HETV productions receiving final certification under the cultural test in the 12 months to September 2026 had a UK production spend of £4.9 billion.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
60 animation television programmes received final certification under the cultural test in the 12 months to September 2026.
There were no co-productions with final certification.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: Animation TV productions receiving final certification under the cultural test in the 12 months to September 2026 had a UK production spend of £177 million.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
76 children’s television programmes received final certification under the cultural test in the 12 months to September 2026.
There were no co-productions with final certification.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: Children’s TV productions receiving final certification under the cultural test in the 12 months to September 2026 had a UK production spend of £205 million.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text:
346 video games received final certification in the 12 months to September 2026.
Video games can only be certified under the cultural test.

title: Screen sector statistics to September 2026
text: Video games receiving final certification in the 12 months to September 2026 had a UK production spend of £0.95 billion.
